findings.message: The class fix for secret-sourced AZDO_ORG/AZDO_PROJECT is tested by one hand-picked row: a project containing a space. AZDO_ORG on the secret path is never varied, because run_entry hard-codes AZDO_ORG=o. The table-driven rows only cover the clone-URL path. Add a secret-path table that varies org and project over a raw space, existing %XX, a lone '%', non-ASCII, '?' and '#', and assert both values.
findings.scenario: If line 38 of entrypoint.sh is changed to encode only AZDO_PROJECT, or the non-URL branch stops encoding AZDO_ORG, a secret value of AZDO_ORG='My Org' with a github.com clone URL reaches the pod unencoded. The suite stays green, because the only secret-path row is ENTRY_PROJECT='My Proj' and it expects org 'o'.

findings.message: AZDO_REPO is spliced into the same in-pod URLs as AZDO_ORG/AZDO_PROJECT, but it is not passed through url_seg. It comes from the raw clone URL tail or a preset secret value. I could not see the consumers, so this holds only if draft-pr, specclaw-azdo-pr and specclaw-azdo-issue do not encode it themselves. If they don't, apply url_seg to AZDO_REPO too.
findings.scenario: FLEET_REPO_URL=https://dev.azure.com/o/p/_git/My Repo gives AZDO_REPO='My Repo'. Unless a consumer encodes it, the PR/issue URL contains a raw space and the call fails, while org and project now encode correctly.
